chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
We have a right. If it is given to us, well and good; otherwise, we will ride on the hind parts of the camels, even if the night journey is long.

key_terms.أَعْجَازَ الْإِبِلِ: hind parts of the camels (a metaphor for enduring hardship or lower status)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the rights of the Ahl al-Bayt and their response to being denied them?
ai.summary: In this famous declaration, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) asserts the inherent right of the Ahl al-Bayt, using the idiom of riding on the 'hind parts of camels' (a'jaz al-ibil) to signify enduring hardship and maintaining dignity while persisting in their claim. This statement underscores the Shia theological principle that their authority is divinely ordained and not merely a political concession, emphasizing resilience in the face of denial. The imagery highlights the contrast between the humility of the claimants and the obstinacy of those who withhold their due rights.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 22. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
We have a right. If it is allowed to us well and good, otherwise, we will ride on the hind part of the camel (like lowly people) even though the night journey may be long.
